claims.quote: Some of the sightings have been attributed to hyperactive imaginations, playful pranks, natural phenomena such as wave action, shadows, lighting effects, logs and a large number of animals

claims.statement: In a quotation carried by the Beacon, most reports other than large-fish sightings describe it as long and eel-shaped, round, 30 to 40 feet in length, with large black eyes.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kutipan yang dimuat Beacon, kebanyakan laporan selain penampakan ikan besar menggambarkannya panjang dan seperti belut, bulat, sepanjang 30 sampai 40 kaki, bermata hitam besar.
claims.quote: Most, other than large fish sightings, describe it as long and eel-shaped, round, 30 to 40 feet in length with large black eyes

claims.statement: According to the Beacon, despite extensive netting, electro-shocking, small submarines and other research, no sign of sturgeon or other creatures has been found.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Beacon, meski ada penjaringan luas, penyetruman listrik, kapal selam kecil, dan penelitian lain, tidak ada tanda ikan sturgeon atau makhluk lain yang ditemukan.
claims.quote: Despite extensive netting, electro-shocking, small submarines that have ventured deep into the lake and other types of research, including time spent underwater in the forks of the Flathead River, no sign of sturgeon or other creatures has been found.

claims.statement: In 1955, C. Leslie Griffith caught a 7.5-foot, 181-pound white sturgeon near Dayton; it was displayed at the Polson museum and fuelled theories that sturgeon might be responsible for the sightings.
claims.statement_id: Pada 1955, C. Leslie Griffith menangkap sturgeon putih 7,5 kaki seberat 181 pon dekat Dayton; ikan itu dipajang di museum Polson dan memicu teori bahwa sturgeon menjadi penyebab penampakan.
claims.quote: In 1955, C. Leslie Griffith captured a 7.5-foot, 181-pound white sturgeon near Dayton. The massive fish was displayed at the Polson-Flathead Historical Museum and fueled theories that sturgeon — rare, deep-dwelling, and prehistoric-looking — might be responsible for the sightings.

claims.statement: According to oral history shared by Kootenai elders Catherine and Louise Andrew, a bird's wife used to feed huckleberries to a friendly lake creature; when her jealous husband found out, he killed the monster.
claims.statement_id: Menurut sejarah lisan dari tetua Kootenai Catherine dan Louise Andrew, istri seekor burung biasa memberi buah huckleberry kepada makhluk danau yang ramah; ketika suaminya yang cemburu mengetahuinya, ia membunuh monster itu.
claims.quote: According to oral history shared by Kootenai elders Catherine and Louise Andrew, a bird’s wife used to feed huckleberries to a friendly lake creature. But when the bird’s jealous husband discovered this, he killed the monster.

claims.statement: The creature's body became what is now called Sullivan Hill, near Elmo on the lake's western shore.
claims.statement_id: Tubuh makhluk itu menjadi bukit yang kini disebut Sullivan Hill, dekat Elmo di tepi barat danau.
claims.quote: The creature’s body became what is now called Sullivan Hill, near Elmo on the lake’s western shore.

claims.statement: In 2024, the city of Polson installed a 25-foot bronze statue of the creature in Sacajawea Park.
claims.statement_id: Pada 2024, kota Polson memasang patung perunggu setinggi 25 kaki makhluk itu di Sacajawea Park.
claims.quote: In 2024, the city of Polson installed a 25-foot bronze statue of the creature in Sacajawea Park

claims.statement: Some sightings identify it as a massive fish between 6 and 10 feet long, possibly a sturgeon.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian penampakan mengidentifikasinya sebagai ikan besar sepanjang 6 sampai 10 kaki, mungkin sturgeon.
claims.quote: Some sightings identify it as a massive fish between 6 and 10 feet in length — possibly a sturgeon.

claims.statement: The Flying Head (also Big Head or the Great Head) is a cannibalistic spirit of Haudenosaunee and Wyandot mythology.
claims.statement_id: Flying Head (juga Big Head atau Great Head) adalah roh kanibal dalam mitologi Haudenosaunee dan Wyandot.
claims.quote: The Flying Head (also known as Big Head or the Great Head) is a cannibalistic spirit from Haudenosaunee and Wyandot mythology.

claims.statement: Flying Heads are ravenous spirits cursed with insatiable hunger.
claims.statement_id: Flying Head digambarkan sebagai roh rakus yang dikutuk dengan kelaparan tak terpuaskan.
claims.quote: Flying Heads are described as being ravenous spirits that are cursed with an insatiable hunger.

claims.statement: They resemble a human head with long dark hair, "terrible eyes" and a large mouth of razor-sharp fangs.
claims.statement_id: Wujudnya seperti kepala manusia berambut gelap panjang, bermata mengerikan, dan bermulut besar penuh taring tajam.
claims.quote: They are generally described as resembling a human head with long dark hair, "terrible eyes", and a large mouth filled with razor sharp fangs.

claims.statement: In some versions it has bat wings at each cheek and bird-like talons.
claims.statement_id: Dalam beberapa versi, ia bersayap kelelawar di kedua pipi dan bercakar seperti burung.
claims.quote: In some versions, the Flying Head has a pair of bat wings jutting from each side of its cheek and bird-like talons.

claims.statement: In all versions it is larger than the tallest man, with a hide no weapon can pierce.
claims.statement_id: Dalam semua versi, ia lebih besar daripada manusia tertinggi dan berkulit yang tak tertembus senjata.
claims.quote: In all instances, they are described as being larger in size than that of the tallest man and possessing a hide that no weapon can penetrate.

claims.statement: According to folklore, the Flying Head drove the original inhabitants near the source of the Hudson River in the Adirondack Mountains from their hunting grounds before Europeans came.
claims.statement_id: Menurut cerita rakyat, Flying Head mengusir penduduk asli dekat hulu Sungai Hudson di Pegunungan Adirondack dari tempat berburu mereka sebelum orang Eropa datang.
claims.quote: the Flying Head drove the original native inhabitants who lived in the area  of the state of New York near the source of the Hudson River, in the Adirondack Mountains away from their hunting grounds before the Europeans came.

claims.statement: Smith writes that among the supernatural beings corresponding to good and evil genii were the Great Heads, with ever watchful eyes and long hair serving as wings to bear them on missions of mercy or of destruction.
claims.statement_id: Smith menulis bahwa di antara makhluk gaib yang sepadan dengan jin baik dan jahat terdapat Great Heads, bermata selalu waspada, dengan rambut panjang yang berfungsi sebagai sayap untuk membawa mereka dalam misi belas kasih atau kehancuran.
claims.quote: Among the supernatural beings corresponding to good and evil genii were the Great Heads, with ever watchful eyes, and long hair which served them as wings to bear them on missions of mercy or of destruction.

claims.statement: Smith records a common belief among Indians in a strange, human-like creature consisting simply of a head, made terrific with large eyes and covered with long hair.
claims.statement_id: Smith mencatat kepercayaan umum di kalangan orang Indian tentang makhluk aneh mirip manusia yang hanya terdiri dari kepala dengan mata besar yang menakutkan dan tertutup rambut panjang.
claims.quote: It was a common belief among Indians that there was a strange, human-like creature, consisting simply of a head made terrific with large eyes and covered with long hair.

claims.statement: According to Smith, the Great Head's home was upon a huge rock, a rifted promontory, over which his long hair streamed in shaggy fierceness.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Smith, kediaman Great Head berada di atas batu besar, sebuah tanjung yang retak, tempat rambut panjangnya terurai lebat.
claims.quote: His home was upon a huge rock, a rifted promontory, over which his long hair streamed in shaggy fierceness.

claims.statement: Smith translates the Great Head's growl on seeing anything with the breath of life as "I see thee, I see thee, thou shalt die," or "thou shalt suffer."
claims.statement_id: Smith menerjemahkan seruan Great Head yang melihat makhluk hidup sebagai "Aku melihatmu, aku melihatmu, kau akan mati" atau "kau akan menderita".
claims.quote: that is, "I see thee, I see thee, thou shalt die," or "thou shalt suffer."

claims.statement: In a story recorded by Smith, the uncle calls the Great Head an awful being who destroys those who go near him.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah yang dicatat Smith, sang paman menyebut Great Head sebagai makhluk mengerikan yang membinasakan orang yang mendekatinya.
claims.quote: He is an awful being, for he destroys those who go near him.

claims.statement: In the same tale, after helping to kill the witch, the Great Head departs, a terrific hurricane arises, and out of the wind he calls the nine brothers to awake, and they all arise to life.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah yang sama, setelah membantu membinasakan penyihir perempuan, Great Head pergi, badai dahsyat bertiup, dan dari dalam angin ia memanggil sembilan bersaudara untuk bangun, lalu mereka semua hidup kembali.
claims.quote: Great Head departed, and then arose a storm and a terrific hurricane, and the Great Head out of the wind called to the nine brothers to awake, and they all arose to life

claims.statement: In Cusick's story as given by Smith, a woman at Onondaga was parching acorns by the fire when one of the monstrous heads appeared at the door; thinking she was eating coals of fire, it disappeared, and none of its kind have been seen since.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah Cusick yang dimuat Smith, seorang perempuan tua di Onondaga sedang memanggang biji ek di dekat api ketika salah satu kepala raksasa muncul di pintu; mengira perempuan itu memakan bara api, kepala itu lenyap, dan sejak itu tidak ada lagi yang terlihat.
claims.quote: An old squaw who resided at Onondaga was alone in her wigwam one evening. While sitting by the fire parching some acorns one of the monstrous heads made its appearance at the door. ... it suddenly disappeared, and none of its kind have been seen since that day.

claims.statement: Smith titles the story "Cusick's story of the dispersion of the Great Heads".
claims.statement_id: Smith memberi kisah itu judul "Cusick's story of the dispersion of the Great Heads" (kisah Cusick tentang tercerai-berainya para Great Head).
claims.quote: CUSICK'S STORY OF THE DISPERSION OF THE GREAT HEADS.

claims.statement: The Fresno nightcrawler is a cryptid said to originate in Fresno, California.
claims.statement_id: Fresno nightcrawler adalah kriptid yang konon berasal dari Fresno, California.
claims.quote: The Fresno nightcrawler is a cryptid said to originate in Fresno, California.

claims.statement: It is described as semi-humanoid, white and long-legged, usually seen in pairs.
claims.statement_id: Ia digambarkan setengah mirip manusia, berwarna putih, berkaki panjang, dan biasanya terlihat berpasangan.
claims.quote: It is described as semi-humanoid, white in color, long-legged, and claimed to be typically spotted in pairs.

claims.statement: They have been compared to "walking pairs of pants".
claims.statement_id: Makhluk ini diibaratkan "celana panjang yang berjalan".
claims.quote: They have been compared to "walking pairs of pants".

claims.statement: According to Brian Dunning, it is an urban legend.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Brian Dunning, Fresno nightcrawler adalah legenda urban.
claims.quote: According to Brian Dunning, the Fresno nightcrawler is an urban legend

claims.statement: It was first popularized by 2007 CCTV footage from south Fresno aired on Univision.
claims.statement_id: Makhluk ini mulai populer lewat rekaman CCTV tahun 2007 dari Fresno selatan yang ditayangkan jaringan televisi Univision.
claims.quote: The Fresno nightcrawler was first popularized by CCTV footage shot in 2007 by a man in south Fresno, California, featured on the television network Univision.

claims.statement: When Michael Banti of Weird Fresno checked with regional tribes, they did not recognize the photographed sculptures as local monuments.
claims.statement_id: Saat Michael Banti dari Weird Fresno menghubungi suku-suku setempat, mereka tidak mengenali patung yang difoto sebagai monumen pribumi setempat.
claims.quote: when Weird Fresno founder Michael Banti contacted regional tribes to confirm their authenticity, his contacts did not recognize the photographed sculptures as matching local indigenous monuments.

claims.statement: It has become an icon of Fresno with merchandise and fans worldwide.
claims.statement_id: Fresno nightcrawler menjadi ikon Fresno dan melahirkan barang dagangan serta penggemar di seluruh dunia.
claims.quote: The Fresno nightcrawler has become an icon of Fresno, and has spawned merchandise and fans around the world.

claims.statement: According to Skeptoid, it looks like a pair of child-sized white sweatpants, pressed flat, walking around by themselves as if worn by some skinny invisible child.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Skeptoid, ia tampak seperti sepasang celana training putih seukuran anak, dipipihkan, yang berjalan sendiri seolah dipakai anak kurus tak kasatmata.
claims.quote: It looks like a pair of child-sized white sweatpants, pressed flat, and walking around by themselves as if worn by some skinny invisible child.

claims.statement: The story began in November 2007 when a man who gave his name only as Jose brought his home security videotape to the Fresno office of Univision, the Spanish-language TV network.
claims.statement_id: Kisah ini bermula pada November 2007, ketika seorang pria yang hanya menyebut namanya Jose membawa rekaman kamera keamanan rumahnya ke kantor Univision, jaringan TV berbahasa Spanyol, di Fresno.
claims.quote: The story got its start way back in November 2007 when a man who gave his name only as Jose ... brought his home security videotape into the Fresno office of Univision, the Spanish-language TV network.

claims.statement: In 2010, the paranormal TV show Fact or Faked did a segment on the video, and its hosts dubbed it the Fresno Nightcrawler.
claims.statement_id: Pada 2010, acara TV paranormal Fact or Faked membuat segmen tentang rekaman itu, dan para pembawanya menamainya Fresno Nightcrawler.
claims.quote: Then in 2010, the paranormal TV show Fact or Faked did a segment on the video. The hosts dubbed it the Fresno Nightcrawler

claims.statement: According to Skeptoid, the videos tend always to show a pair of them, one taller and one shorter.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Skeptoid, video-video itu cenderung selalu memperlihatkan sepasang, satu lebih tinggi dan satu lebih pendek.
claims.quote: The videos tend to always show a pair of them, one taller and one shorter.

claims.statement: Jose showed a visitor the yard where the video was taken, and it was clear the creatures had been quite small, no more than half a meter high.
claims.statement_id: Jose menunjukkan halaman tempat video direkam, dan jelas bahwa sosok-sosok itu cukup kecil, tidak lebih dari setengah meter tingginya.
claims.quote: Jose showed him the yard where the video was taken and it was clear that the creatures had been quite small, no more than half a meter high.

claims.statement: According to Skeptoid, the number of people who firmly and passionately believe the Fresno Nightcrawler must be an actual undiscovered species probably approaches zero.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Skeptoid, jumlah orang yang teguh percaya bahwa Fresno Nightcrawler pasti spesies yang belum ditemukan mungkin mendekati nol.
claims.quote: The number of people who firmly and passionately believe that the Fresno Nightcrawler must represent an actual undiscovered species probably approaches zero.

claims.statement: According to Skeptoid, almost nobody actually believes it is a real creature and its backstory is unremarkable, yet it has a prodigious community of supporters likely to keep growing.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Skeptoid, hampir tidak ada orang yang sungguh percaya makhluk ini nyata dan latar ceritanya tidak istimewa, namun ia punya komunitas pendukung besar yang kemungkinan terus bertambah.
claims.quote: The Fresno Nightcrawler is supported by little or no actual belief by anyone that it's a real creature; there's nothing particularly thought-provoking in its backstory; and yet, it has a prodigious community of supporters that is only likely to continue growing.

claims.statement: The gallinipper is a cryptid of African-American folk tradition.
claims.statement_id: Gallinipper adalah kriptid dalam tradisi rakyat Afrika-Amerika.
claims.quote: The gallinipper is a cryptid in the African-American folk tradition.

claims.statement: They were said to be giant mosquitoes whose bones could fence a 140-acre field.
claims.statement_id: Makhluk ini konon nyamuk raksasa yang tulangnya cukup untuk memagari ladang seluas 140 acre.
claims.quote: These creatures were said to be a species of giant mosquitoes so big that their bones could fence a 140-acre (57 ha) field.

claims.statement: In a popular telling it pulls its bill from a tree trunk, clearing 140 acres in the struggle.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah populer, makhluk ini menarik paruhnya dari batang pohon dan membersihkan lahan 140 acre selama meronta.
claims.quote: A popular telling of the legends has the creature get its bill out of a tree trunk, with the animal being large enough to clear 140 acres of land during the struggle.

claims.statement: Gallinipper tales were taken up in minstrel shows and appear in blues songs such as "Mosquito Moan" by Blind Lemon Jefferson.
claims.statement_id: Kisah gallinipper diambil untuk pertunjukan minstrel, tetapi juga muncul dalam lagu blues seperti "Mosquito Moan" karya Blind Lemon Jefferson.
claims.quote: Gallinipper tales were appropriated as a feature of minstrel shows, but have also appeared in American blues songs such as "Mosquito Moan" by Blind Lemon Jefferson

claims.statement: According to Merriam-Webster, gallinipper is chiefly Southern US and Midland US usage for any of various insects, such as a large mosquito or crane fly.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Merriam-Webster, gallinipper dipakai terutama di Southern US dan Midland US untuk berbagai serangga, seperti nyamuk besar (large mosquito) atau crane fly.
claims.quote: chiefly Southern US and Midland US : any of various insects (such as a large mosquito or crane fly)

claims.statement: Merriam-Webster records the earlier forms gurnipper and gal-knipper, and says the word is of obscure origin.
claims.statement_id: Merriam-Webster mencatat bentuk yang lebih awal gurnipper dan gal-knipper, dan asal katanya tidak jelas.
claims.quote: earlier gurnipper, gal-knipper, of obscure origin

claims.statement: Fauset records a short tale in which the narrator says a gallinipper came after him down Mobile way, ran behind a tree and through it, and he clinched it on the other side.
claims.statement_id: Fauset mencatat sebuah kisah singkat: seorang penutur mengaku seekor gallinipper mengejarnya di daerah Mobile, berlari di balik pohon dan menembus pohon itu, lalu ia mendekapnya dari sisi lain.
claims.quote: A gallinipper come after me down Mobile way. He run behind that tree. The gallinipper come th’oo the tree. I clinched on the other side. I had him.

claims.statement: Gaoh (also Ga-oh) is a wind spirit and giant of the Haudenosaunee, Wendat and Seneca.
claims.statement_id: Gaoh (juga Ga-oh) adalah roh angin dan raksasa orang Haudenosaunee, Wendat, dan Seneca.
claims.quote: Gaoh, Ga-oh or Gǎ-oh is a wind spirit and giant of the Haudenosaunee, Wendat and Seneca people.

claims.statement: Gaoh was described as a cannibal giant who could uproot trees, taking the form of a solitary old man.
claims.statement_id: Gaoh digambarkan sebagai raksasa kanibal yang dapat mencabut pohon, berwujud lelaki tua yang menyendiri.
claims.quote: Gaoh was described as a cannibal and a giant who could uproot trees. He takes the form of a solitary old man.

claims.statement: Gaoh is subservient to the Great Spirit and, in Haudenosaunee mythology, to Adekagagwaa.
claims.statement_id: Gaoh tunduk kepada Roh Agung, dan dalam mitologi Haudenosaunee ia tunduk kepada Adekagagwaa.
claims.quote: Gaoh is subservient to the Great Spirit, and in Haudenosaunee mythology he is subservient to Adekagagwaa.

claims.statement: Gaoh is mostly benevolent but can be restless and violent, creating storms.
claims.statement_id: Gaoh umumnya roh baik, tetapi bisa gelisah, ganas, dan menciptakan badai.
claims.quote: Gaoh is mostly a benevolent spirit, but can be restless and violent, and would create storms.

claims.statement: From his home he controls the seasons and the winds of the four directions.
claims.statement_id: Dari rumahnya, ia mengendalikan musim dan angin dari empat penjuru mata angin.
claims.quote: From his home, he controls the seasons, and also winds of the four cardinal directions

claims.statement: His winds are Ya-o-gah (Bear, north), Da-jo-ji (Panther, west), O-yan-do-ne (Moose, east) and Ne-o-gah (Fawn, south).
claims.statement_id: Angin-anginnya adalah Ya-o-gah (beruang angin utara), Da-jo-ji (macan kumbang angin barat), O-yan-do-ne (rusa besar angin timur), dan Ne-o-gah (anak rusa angin selatan).
claims.quote: Ya-o-gah ... or Bear of the north wind, Da-jo-ji ... or Panther of the west wind, O-yan-do-ne ... or Moose of the east wind and Ne-o-gah ... or Fawn of the south wind.

claims.statement: In the Seneca version, Gaoh is chained to a rock, and winds blow when he tries to break free.
claims.statement_id: Dalam versi Seneca, Gaoh dirantai ke batu, dan angin bertiup saat ia berusaha melepaskan diri.
claims.quote: In the Seneca version of the myth, Gaoh is chained to a rock, and winds would blow when he attempts to break free.

claims.statement: Though of giant proportions, Ga-oh, who governs the winds, is confined in the broad north sky.
claims.statement_id: Meski bertubuh raksasa, Ga-oh, yang menguasai angin, dikurung di langit utara yang luas.
claims.quote: Though of giant proportions, Ga-oh ... who governs the winds, is confined in the broad north sky.

claims.statement: Were Ga-oh free, he would tear the heavens into fragments.
claims.statement_id: Seandainya Ga-oh bebas, ia akan mencabik langit menjadi serpihan.
claims.quote: Were Ga-oh free, he would tear the heavens into fragments.

claims.statement: Ga-oh is not an evil being, however his four winds may rage; on the contrary he is solicitous for the welfare of men and ever obedient to the commands of the Creator.
claims.statement_id: Ga-oh bukan makhluk jahat, seganas apa pun keempat anginnya; sebaliknya ia peduli pada kesejahteraan manusia dan selalu menaati perintah Sang Pencipta.
claims.quote: Ga-oh is not an evil being, howsoever his four winds may rage, but on the contrary, solicitous for the welfare of men and ever obedient to the commands of the Creator.

claims.statement: In a footnote the writer states, from her researches, that Ga-oh dwells in the west sky, agreeing with Morgan, who names the western sky as the abode of the wind spirit and calls his dwelling Da-yo-da-do-go-wa.
claims.statement_id: Dalam catatan kaki, penulis menyatakan berdasarkan penelitiannya bahwa Ga-oh tinggal di langit barat, sejalan dengan Morgan yang menyebut langit barat sebagai tempat tinggal roh angin dan menamai kediamannya Da-yo-da-do-go-wa.
claims.quote: Ga-oh dwells in the west sky according to the researches of the writer, agreeing with Morgan who names the western sky as the abode of the wind spirit and calls his dwelling Da-yo-da-do-go-wa.

claims.statement: At the entrance of his abode are four watchers: the Bear (north wind), Panther (west wind), Moose (east wind) and Fawn (south wind).
claims.statement_id: Di pintu kediamannya ada empat penjaga: Beruang (angin utara), Macan Kumbang (angin barat), Rusa Besar (angin timur), dan Anak Rusa (angin selatan).
claims.quote: the Bear (north wind). Panther (west wind). Moose (east wind), and Fawn (south wind).

claims.statement: When Ga-oh is contented and happy, gentle and invigorating breezes fan Earth.
claims.statement_id: Ketika Ga-oh puas dan bahagia, angin sepoi-sepoi yang lembut dan menyegarkan berembus ke Bumi.
claims.quote: When Ga-oh is contented and happy, gentle and invigorating breezes fan Earth

claims.statement: A footnote says that Ga-oh is the name of the wind spirit according to Morgan.
claims.statement_id: Dalam catatan kaki disebutkan bahwa Ga-oh adalah nama roh angin menurut Morgan.
claims.quote: Ga-oh is the name of the wind spirit according to Morgan.

claims.statement: Depending on the myths, he either lives in a house in the sky or in a mountain cave called "the House of Winds."
claims.statement_id: Tergantung mitosnya, ia tinggal di rumah di langit atau di gua gunung bernama "Rumah Angin".
claims.quote: Depending on the myths, he either lives in a house in the sky, or a mountain cave called "the House of Winds."

claims.statement: Some versions of the myths describe the winds as the guardians of Gaoh's home, while others describe them as locked up in his home, to be released once Gaoh receives the order from the Great Spirit.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian versi mitos menggambarkan angin sebagai penjaga rumah Gaoh, sementara versi lain menggambarkan angin terkunci di rumahnya dan akan dilepaskan setelah Gaoh menerima perintah dari Roh Agung.
claims.quote: Some versions of the myths describe the winds as the guardians of Gaoh's home, while others describe the winds being locked up in his home, who were to be released once Gaoh receives the order from the Great Spirit.

claims.statement: Guahaioque was a minor deity of the Muisca religion, god of evil, stealing, lies and death.
claims.statement_id: Guahaioque adalah dewa minor dalam agama Muisca, dewa kejahatan, pencurian, kebohongan, dan kematian.
claims.quote: Guahaioque was a minor deity in the religion of the Muisca. It was the god of evil, stealing, lies and death.

claims.statement: In the Muisca language, Muysccubun, the name means "figure of the deceased".
claims.statement_id: Dalam bahasa Muisca, Muysccubun, nama Guahaioque berarti "sosok orang yang telah meninggal".
claims.quote: The name Guahaioque in the language of the Muisca, Muysccubun, means "figure of the deceased".

claims.statement: The name lives on as that of a folk metal band from Cali.
claims.statement_id: Nama Guahaioque kini dipakai oleh sebuah band folk metal dari Cali.
claims.quote: The name Guahaioque lives on as the name of a folk metal band from Cali.

claims.statement: The Muysca-Spanish dictionary defines guahaioque as a noun meaning "demonio, diablo" (literally "figura de difunto").
claims.statement_id: Kamus Muysca-Spanyol mendefinisikan guahaioque sebagai kata benda yang berarti "demonio, diablo" (secara harfiah "figura de difunto").
claims.quote: I. s. Demonio, diablo ( lit. "figura de difunto". )

claims.statement: The dictionary cites a manuscript identified as Ms. 158 (Voc.), in which "demonio" is rendered guahaioque (fol. 53r) and "diablo" guhaioque (fol. 59r).
claims.statement_id: Kamus mengutip naskah yang disebut Ms. 158 (Voc.), tempat "demonio" dipadankan dengan guahaioque (fol. 53r) dan "diablo" dengan guhaioque (fol. 59r).
claims.quote: Demonio = guahaioque = [sic] (Gómez & Torres, 2013) - Ms. 158. Voc. fol. 53r Diablo = guhaioque = [sic] (Gómez & Torres, 2013) - Ms. 158. Voc. fol. 59r

claims.statement: The dictionary entry gives the spellings guahaioque and guhaioque and the morphological analysis guahaia-uque.
claims.statement_id: Entri kamus memuat ejaan guahaioque dan guhaioque serta uraian morfologis guahaia-uque.
claims.quote: guahaioque, guhaioque Fon. Gonz.*/ɣuahaioke/ Cons. */ɣuahaioke/ Morf. guahaia-uque

claims.statement: Guaraci or Quaraci (from Tupi kûarasý, "sun") is the Sun god of Guaraní mythology, creator of all living creatures.
claims.statement_id: Guaraci atau Quaraci (dari kata Tupi kûarasý, "matahari") adalah dewa Matahari dalam mitologi Guaraní, pencipta semua makhluk hidup.
claims.quote: Guaraci or Quaraci (from Tupi kûarasý, "sun") in the Guaraní mythology is the god of the Sun, creator of all living creatures.

claims.statement: According to Cascudo, Coaraci is the Sun in the Tupi or Nheengatu language, from coá "this", ara "day" and ci "mother": "mother of this day", "mother of the day", the explanation of the origin of daylight.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Cascudo, Coaraci adalah Matahari dalam bahasa Tupi atau nheengatu, dari coá "ini", ara "hari", dan ci "ibu": "ibu hari ini", "ibu sang hari", penjelasan asal cahaya siang.
claims.quote: Coaraci. O Sol no idioma tupi, ou nheengatu. De coá, este, ara dia, ci, mãe deste dia, mãe do dia, a explica- ção da origem da luz diurna.

claims.statement: In the Guaraci entry, Cascudo writes that Couto de Magalhães, who devised an indigenous theogony, stated that the Sun is the creator of all living things, in charge of directing the animal kingdom.
claims.statement_id: Dalam verbet Guaraci, Cascudo menulis bahwa Couto de Magalhães, yang menyusun sebuah teogoni pribumi, menyatakan Matahari adalah pencipta semua makhluk hidup dan bertugas memimpin dunia hewan.
claims.quote: Guaraci. Couto de Magalhães, que arquitetara uma teogonia indígena, escreveu que o Sol é o criador de todos os viventes, encarregado de dirigir o reino animal

claims.statement: In that theogony, subject to Coaraci live Anhangá, protecting the game of the open field, Caapora, that of the forest, Guirapuru, the birds, and Uauiará, the fish.
claims.statement_id: Dalam teogoni itu, di bawah Coaraci hidup Anhangá yang melindungi buruan padang, Caapora yang melindungi buruan hutan, Guirapuru yang melindungi burung, dan Uauiará yang melindungi ikan.
claims.quote: Sujeitos a Coaraci, com o domí- nio sobre os seres privativos de sua jurisdição, vivem Anhangá, protegen- do a caça do campo, Caapora, a do mato, Guirapuru, os pássaros, Uauia- rá, os peixes.

claims.statement: In that theogony, Coaraci's sister and wife is Jaci, the Moon, who likewise has her court with functions identical to her brother's.
claims.statement_id: Dalam teogoni itu, saudari sekaligus istri Coaraci adalah Jaci, sang Bulan, yang juga memiliki istana dengan fungsi yang sama dengan saudaranya.
claims.quote: A irmã e esposa do Coa- raci é Jaci, a Lua, tendo semelhante- mente sua corte, com funções idênti- cas às do seu irmão.

claims.statement: Cascudo writes that there are no traces supporting the existence of an astral cult among the indigenous peoples of Brazil, and that they had no devotion to the Sun.
claims.statement_id: Cascudo menulis bahwa tidak ada jejak yang mendukung adanya pemujaan benda langit di kalangan masyarakat pribumi Brasil, dan bahwa mereka tidak memiliki pengabdian apa pun kepada Matahari.
claims.quote: Não há vestígios que fundarmentem a existência de um culto astrolátrico entre os indígenas do Brasil. Os indígenas nenhuma de- voção possuíam para o Sol

claims.statement: According to Cascudo, Stradelli says the form Coraci was heard pronounced in Pará and the lower Amazon.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Cascudo, Stradelli mengatakan bentuk Coraci terdengar diucapkan di Pará dan Amazonas hilir.
claims.quote: Stradelli diz que se ouvia pronunciar Coraci no Pará e baixo Amazonas.

claims.statement: In the Jaci entry, Cascudo describes Jaci as sister and wife of the Sun in the indigenous theogony, the Sun being named Coaraci, Coraci, Goaraci or Gorazi.
claims.statement_id: Dalam verbet Jaci, Cascudo menyebut Jaci sebagai saudari dan istri sang Matahari dalam teogoni pribumi, dengan nama Coaraci, Coraci, Goaraci, atau Gorazi.
claims.quote: Na teogonia indígena era irmã e ca- sada com o Sol, Coaraci, Coraci, Goa- raci, Gorazi.

claims.statement: In New York folklore, the Hudson River Monster ("Kipsy", also "Keepsie" or "Libby") is a serpentine water monster reported along the Hudson River and New York Harbor since 1886.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat New York, Hudson River Monster ("Kipsy", juga "Keepsie" atau "Libby") adalah monster air mirip ular yang dilaporkan terlihat di Sungai Hudson dan Pelabuhan New York sejak 1886.
claims.quote: In New York folklore, the Hudson River Monster, popularly known as "Kipsy" or less commonly "Keepsie" or "Libby" (after the Statue of Liberty) is an aquatic serpentine monster reportedly spotted along the Hudson River and New York Harbor since 1886.

claims.statement: The name "Kipsy" is believed to come from Poughkeepsie, a city on the river.
claims.statement_id: Nama "Kipsy" diyakini berasal dari Poughkeepsie, kota di tepi sungai itu.
claims.quote: The name "Kipsy" is believed to derive from Poughkeepsie, a city located along the river.

claims.statement: It was first reported in 1886 newspaper articles that called it simply "the sea serpent."
claims.statement_id: Makhluk ini pertama kali dilaporkan dalam serangkaian artikel surat kabar tahun 1886 yang menyebutnya "ular laut".
claims.quote: The creature was first reported in a series of newspaper articles published in 1886, in which it is referred to simply as "the sea serpent."

claims.statement: Many sources claim Kipsy appears in Native American legends or was seen by Henry Hudson's crew, but none provide documentation.
claims.statement_id: Banyak sumber menyebut Kipsy ada dalam legenda pribumi atau dilihat awak Henry Hudson, tetapi tidak ada yang menyertakan bukti dokumen.
claims.quote: Though many sources allege that "Kipsy" was described in Native American legends or spotted by Henry Hudson's crew as the sailed up the Hudson River on the Halve Maen, none provide any documentation in support of these claims.

claims.statement: According to this encyclopedia, Kipsy is named for Poughkeepsie, and its local legends tell of an ancient creature that many sailors spotted on the Hudson River, described as a shark, manatee, sea serpent, or dinosaur.
claims.statement_id: Menurut ensiklopedia ini, Kipsy dinamai dari kota Poughkeepsie, dan legenda setempat bercerita tentang makhluk purba yang dilihat banyak pelaut di Sungai Hudson, digambarkan sebagai hiu, manatee, ular laut, atau dinosaurus.
claims.quote: Poughkeepsie is the city for which Kipsy is named, and its local legends talk about an ancient creature that many sailors spotted on the Hudson River, describing the creature as a shark, manatee, sea serpent, or dinosaur.

claims.statement: In 1886, dozens of people insisted they had seen a 100-foot-long sea serpent with a huge head in the Hudson River, repeatedly rearing as high as ten feet in the air.
claims.statement_id: Pada 1886, puluhan orang bersikeras telah melihat ular laut sepanjang 100 kaki berkepala besar di Sungai Hudson yang berulang kali menegak setinggi sepuluh kaki ke udara.
claims.quote: In 1886 dozens of people insisted they had seen a 100-foot-long sea serpent with a huge head in the Hudson River repeatedly rearing as high as ten feet in the air.

claims.statement: According to this encyclopedia, the so-called monster was identified as a burned timber from the steamship Daniel Drew.
claims.statement_id: Menurut ensiklopedia ini, makhluk yang disebut-sebut itu akhirnya diidentifikasi sebagai balok kayu terbakar dari kapal uap Daniel Drew.
claims.quote: As it turned out, the so-called monster was identified as a burned timber from the steamship Daniel Drew.

claims.statement: Kipsy reappeared in the New York Times in 2006 when witnesses at Chelsea Piers, Westchester County, and Kingsland Point in Sleepy Hollow reported seeing a manatee weighing 1,000 pounds.
claims.statement_id: Kipsy muncul kembali di New York Times pada 2006 ketika saksi di Chelsea Piers, Westchester County, dan Kingsland Point di Sleepy Hollow melaporkan telah melihat manatee seberat 1.000 pon.
claims.quote: Kipsy reappeared in the New York Times in 2006 when witnesses at Chelsea Piers, Westchester County, and Kingsland Point in Sleepy Hollow reported that they had seen a manatee with a weight of 1,000 pounds.

claims.statement: According to this encyclopedia, the only images of Kipsy that exist are paintings, because no one has succeeded in photographing the lake monster.
claims.statement_id: Menurut ensiklopedia ini, satu-satunya gambar Kipsy yang ada adalah lukisan, karena belum ada yang berhasil memotret monster danau itu.
claims.quote: So far, the only images of Kipsy that exist are paintings because no one has been successful in photographing the lake monster.

claims.statement: A Poughkeepsie mural by local artists Margaret and Richard Crenson on the Hudson Valley Office Furniture building in 1989 shows Kipsy as a mythical serpent living in the Hudson River.
claims.statement_id: Mural di Poughkeepsie karya seniman lokal Margaret dan Richard Crenson pada gedung Hudson Valley Office Furniture tahun 1989 menampilkan Kipsy sebagai ular mitos yang hidup di Sungai Hudson.
claims.quote: a Poughkeepsie mural created by local artists Margaret and Richard Crenson on the Hudson Valley Office Furniture building in 1989 shows Kipsy as a mythical serpent living in the Hudson River.

claims.statement: In her 2009 visual artwork series Bodice of the Goddess—The Secret Life of the Hudson River, American artist Carla Goldberg portrayed Kipsy playing ball with one of the river goddess's heads.
claims.statement_id: Dalam serial karya seni visualnya tahun 2009, Bodice of the Goddess—The Secret Life of the Hudson River, seniman Amerika Carla Goldberg menggambarkan Kipsy bermain bola dengan salah satu kepala dewi sungai.
claims.quote: In her 2009 visual artwork series Bodice of the Goddess—The Secret Life of the Hudson River, American artist Carla Goldberg portrayed Kipsy as playing ball with one of the river goddess’s heads.

claims.statement: In Mi'kmaq folklore, a Jenu is a wild, cannibalistic hairy giant.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Mi'kmaq, Jenu adalah raksasa berbulu yang liar dan kanibal.
claims.quote: In Miꞌkmaq folklore, a Jenu is a wild and cannibalistic hairy giant.

claims.statement: A Jenu is created when a human "allows ice into their heart".
claims.statement_id: Jenu tercipta ketika seseorang "membiarkan es masuk ke hatinya".
claims.quote: Jenu are created when a human "allows ice into their heart".

claims.statement: Once transformed, Jenu look hairy and emaciated, with bones poking through the skin.
claims.statement_id: Setelah berubah, Jenu tampak berbulu dan kurus kering dengan tulang mencuat dari kulit.
claims.quote: Once transformed, Jenu appear hairy and emaciated, with bones poking through the skin.

claims.statement: Jenu are most active in winter, when humans move less and are easier to hunt.
claims.statement_id: Jenu paling aktif pada musim dingin karena manusia kurang bergerak dan lebih mudah diburu.
claims.quote: Jenu are most active during the winter because humans move less and are easier to hunt.

claims.statement: Jenu are comparable to the Wendigo of Anishinaabe and Cree mythology and, less so, to Sasquatch.
claims.statement_id: Jenu dapat dibandingkan dengan Wendigo dalam mitologi Anishinaabe dan Cree, dan sedikit dengan Sasquatch.
claims.quote: Jenua are comparable to the Wendigo of Anishinaabe and Cree mythology (and, to a lesser extent, Sasquatch).

claims.statement: Micmac religious belief is highly syncretic, and non-Christian supernatural beings live on alongside Christian belief; these include Kukwes, a giant cannibal, Wiklatmuj, little forest people, and Jenu, northern ice giants.
claims.statement_id: Kepercayaan Micmac sangat sinkretis, dan makhluk gaib non-Kristen juga tetap hidup berdampingan dengan kepercayaan Kristen; di antaranya Kukwes, raksasa kanibal, Wiklatmuj, manusia kecil hutan, dan Jenu, raksasa es dari utara.
claims.quote: Micmac religious belief is highly syncretic, and other non-Christian supernatural beings also live on in tandem with Christian belief. These include Kukwes, a giant cannibal, Wiklatmuj, little forest people, Jenu, northern ice giants,

claims.statement: The page lists Jenu, Cenu, Chenu, Jinu, Cinu, Djenu, Chinu, Cheno and Tsi-noo as alternate spellings of the name Chenoo, with tribal affiliation Micmac, Maliseet and Passamaquoddy.
claims.statement_id: Halaman ini mencantumkan Jenu, Cenu, Chenu, Jinu, Cinu, Djenu, Chinu, Cheno, dan Tsi-noo sebagai ejaan lain dari nama Chenoo, dengan afiliasi suku Micmac, Maliseet, dan Passamaquoddy.
claims.quote: Name: Chenoo Tribal affiliation: Micmac, Maliseet, Passamaquoddy Alternate spellings: Jenu, Cenu, Chenu, Jinu, Cinu, Djenu, Chinu, Cheno, Chenu, Tsi-noo

claims.statement: Chenoos are the evil man-eating ice giants of northern Wabanaki legends; a Chenoo was once a human who became possessed by an evil spirit or committed a terrible crime (especially cannibalism or withholding food from a starving person), causing his heart to turn to ice.
claims.statement_id: Chenoo adalah raksasa es pemakan manusia yang jahat dalam legenda Wabanaki utara; dahulu ia manusia yang dirasuki roh jahat atau melakukan kejahatan berat (terutama kanibalisme atau menolak memberi makan orang yang kelaparan), sehingga hatinya menjadi es.
claims.quote: Chenoos are the evil man-eating ice giants of northern Wabanaki legends. A Chenoo was once a human being who either became possessed by an evil spirit or committed a terrible crime (especially cannibalism or withholding food from a starving person), causing his heart to turn to ice.

claims.statement: In a few legends a human has been successfully rescued from the frozen heart of a Chenoo, but usually once a person has been transformed into a Chenoo, their only escape is death.
claims.statement_id: Dalam beberapa legenda, manusia berhasil diselamatkan dari hati beku seorang Chenoo, tetapi biasanya setelah seseorang berubah menjadi Chenoo, satu-satunya jalan keluar adalah kematian.
claims.quote: In a few legends a human has been successfully rescued from the frozen heart of a Chenoo, but usually once a person has been transformed into a Chenoo, their only escape is death.

claims.statement: The page lists related figures in other tribes: Kee-wakw (Abenaki), Windigo (Anishinabe) and Wihtiko (Cree).
claims.statement_id: Halaman ini mencantumkan tokoh terkait di suku lain: Kee-wakw (Abenaki), Windigo (Anishinabe), dan Wihtiko (Cree).
claims.quote: Related figures in other tribes: Kee-wakw (Abenaki), Windigo (Anishinabe), Wihtiko (Cree)

claims.statement: La Bolefuego (or La Candileja) is a legendary character of Colombian and Venezuelan folklore.
claims.statement_id: La Bolefuego (atau La Candileja) adalah tokoh legenda dari cerita rakyat Kolombia dan Venezuela.
claims.quote: La Bolefuego (or La Candileja) is a legendary character from Colombian and Venezuelan folklore.

claims.statement: It is a bright apparition of the dark nights of Los Llanos, like a flashing lantern that spins and shakes violently.
claims.statement_id: Ia konon penampakan terang pada malam gelap di Los Llanos, digambarkan seperti lentera berkedip yang berputar dan berguncang keras.
claims.quote: It is said to be a bright apparition, found in the dark nights of Los Llanos. It is described as a flashing lantern that turns and shakes violently.

claims.statement: The Bolefuego is said to be the spirit of a woman burned alive at home with her two children; she attacks travelers.
claims.statement_id: Bolefuego konon arwah perempuan yang terbakar hidup-hidup di rumahnya bersama dua anaknya; ia menyerang para pelancong.
claims.quote: The Bolefuego is said to be the spirit of a woman that was burned alive in her home, along with her two children. She attacks travelers.

claims.statement: Those facing her are told not to pray; unlike other evil beings, she is attracted by prayers.
claims.statement_id: Orang yang berhadapan dengannya dianjurkan tidak berdoa, karena berbeda dengan makhluk jahat lain, Bolefuego justru tertarik oleh doa.
claims.quote: Those facing her are advised not to pray; unlike other evil entities, the Bolefuego is attracted by prayers.

claims.statement: According to this folklore book on Portuguesa state, many beliefs are woven around the Bola de Fuego's origin: the soul in torment of a sinful bishop, a son who cursed his mother, two comadres who quarreled on Holy Thursday, the wandering Jew, the tyrant Aguirre, or the wandering spirit of a loving couple who made love during Holy Week.
claims.statement_id: Menurut buku folklor negara bagian Portuguesa ini, asal-usul Bola de Fuego diceritakan dalam banyak kepercayaan: jiwa gentayangan seorang uskup berdosa, seorang anak yang mengutuk ibunya, dua comadre yang bertengkar pada Kamis Putih, Yahudi pengembara, tiran Aguirre, atau roh pengembara sepasang kekasih yang bercinta pada hari-hari Pekan Suci.
claims.quote: Sobre su origen se tejen muchas creencias, entre ellas que se trata del alma en pena de un obispo pecador, de un hijo que maldijo a su madre, de dos comadres que pelearon un jueves santo, del judío errante, del tirano Aguirre, o del espíritu vagante de una pareja enamorada que hizo el amor en los días de la Semana Santa.

claims.statement: There is no specific zone of Portuguesa where the Bola de Fuego or bola de candela can be located; it comes and goes across the whole state, even all corners of the Venezuelan plains.
claims.statement_id: Tidak ada zona khusus di Portuguesa tempat Bola de Fuego (bola de candela) bisa dipastikan; ia berkeliaran di seluruh wilayah negara bagian itu, bahkan di setiap sudut dataran Venezuela.
claims.quote: No hay una zona específica de Portuguesa donde se pueda ubicar la Bola de Fuego o bola de candela, ella anda y desanda por toda la geografía del estado, e incluso por todos los rincones del llano venezolano.

claims.statement: In one testimony, if one looks at it fixedly it looks like a person burning inside with open arms as if begging for mercy; the older women began to curse it and swear at it, and it began to move away.
claims.statement_id: Dalam salah satu kesaksian, jika dipandang lekat-lekat ia tampak seperti seseorang yang menyala di dalamnya dengan lengan terbuka seolah memohon belas kasihan; para perempuan yang lebih tua mulai mengutuk dan memakinya, lalu ia menjauh.
claims.quote: Si uno la mira fijo se ve como una persona prendida adentro, se ven los brazos abiertos como pidiendo clemencia. Yo recuerdo que las mujeres más grandes comenzaron a maldecirla y a decirle groserías y ella comenzó a alejarse.

claims.statement: In another testimony, when a man among them started praying to it, the uncle told him to stop because those are lost souls, and the more one prays to them the more they stick to one from behind.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kesaksian lain, ketika seorang pria di antara mereka mulai berdoa kepadanya, sang paman menyuruhnya berhenti karena itu adalah arwah-arwah tersesat, dan semakin didoakan semakin ia menempel di belakang mereka.
claims.quote: un señor que andaba con nosotros se puso a rezarle y mi tío le dijo: Dejá de está rezando que esas son ánimas perdidas que andan desandando y mientras más le recéis más se nos va a pegar atrás.

claims.statement: In another testimony, the ball of fire or light was a strange object that gave off no heat but lit the whole road.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kesaksian lain, bola api atau cahaya itu adalah benda aneh yang tidak menghasilkan panas tetapi menerangi seluruh jalan.
claims.quote: Esta bola de candela o de luz era un objeto extraño, no producía ningún calor, pero sí nos alumbraba todo el camino.

claims.statement: One witness says he was not afraid because his parents had told him about it and never said it did harm.
claims.statement_id: Seorang saksi menyatakan ia tidak takut karena orang tuanya pernah bercerita tentangnya dan tidak pernah mengatakan bahwa ia berbahaya.
claims.quote: A mí no me dio miedo porque mis padres me habían hablado de ella y jamás me dijeron que hacía daño.

claims.statement: One witness reports that scientists say the phenomenon is accumulated gases that produce light or an explosion, but having seen it himself he cannot believe that.
claims.statement_id: Seorang saksi menyebut bahwa para ilmuwan mengatakan fenomena itu adalah gas yang terakumulasi dan menimbulkan cahaya atau ledakan, tetapi karena telah melihatnya sendiri ia tidak dapat mempercayainya.
claims.quote: Por haber visto este fenómeno yo no puedo creer en el concepto de lo que dicen los científicos: que son gases acumulados que hacen luz o explosión.

claims.statement: La Diablesse is a figure of Caribbean folklore; she was an enslaved African woman who gave her soul to the Devil for eternal beauty, becoming a demi-human.
claims.statement_id: La Diablesse adalah tokoh cerita rakyat Karibia; menurut kisahnya, ia perempuan Afrika yang diperbudak dan menyerahkan jiwanya kepada Iblis demi kecantikan abadi, lalu menjadi setengah manusia.
claims.quote: is a character in Caribbean folklore. According to folklore, she was an enslaved African woman who made a deal with Le Diable (the Devil) to give her soul to him, becoming a demi-human, in exchange for eternal beauty.

claims.statement: Her hideous face is hidden by a wide hat, and her long dress hides one leg ending in a cow hoof.
claims.statement_id: Wajahnya yang mengerikan tersembunyi di balik topi lebar, dan gaun panjangnya menutupi satu kaki yang berujung kuku sapi.
claims.quote: However, her hideous face is hidden by a large brimmed hat, and her long dress hides the fact that one leg ends in a cow hoof.

claims.statement: She can bewitch an unsuspecting male victim, lead him into the forest and then vanish.
claims.statement_id: Ia dapat menyihir korban laki-laki dan membawanya ke hutan, lalu menghilang.
claims.quote: She can cast spells on her unsuspecting male victim, whom she leads into the forest. When in the forest, she disappears.

claims.statement: The confused, lost victim runs through the forest until he falls into a ravine or river, or is eaten.
claims.statement_id: Korban yang bingung dan tersesat berlarian di hutan sampai jatuh ke jurang atau sungai, atau dimangsa.
claims.quote: The victim (confused, lost, and scared) runs around the forest until he falls into a ravine or river, or gets eaten.

claims.statement: Derek Walcott refers to La Diablesse in his play Dream on Monkey Mountain.
claims.statement_id: Derek Walcott menyebut La Diablesse dalam dramanya Dream on Monkey Mountain.
claims.quote: La Diablesse is referred by Derek Walcott in his play Dream on Monkey Mountain.

claims.statement: The book Two Years in the French West Indies is by Lafcadio Hearn.
claims.statement_id: Buku Two Years in the French West Indies ditulis oleh Lafcadio Hearn.
claims.quote: Title: Two Years in the French West Indies Author: Lafcadio Hearn

claims.statement: Hearn writes that the "guiablesse" (in Bitaco idiom) represents a singular Martinique superstition: it is said that sometimes at noonday a beautiful woman passes silently through an isolated plantation, smiling at the workers in the cane-fields and tempting men to follow her, and he who follows her never comes back.
claims.statement_id: Hearn menulis bahwa "guiablesse" (dalam ungkapan Bitaco) mewakili takhayul khas Martinik: konon kadang pada tengah hari seorang perempuan cantik lewat diam-diam di perkebunan terpencil, tersenyum kepada para pekerja ladang tebu dan menggoda laki-laki agar mengikutinya, dan yang mengikutinya tidak pernah kembali.
claims.quote: The deviless (in true Bitaco idiom, "guiablesse") represents a singular Martinique superstition. It is said that sometimes at noonday, a beautiful negress passes silently through some isolated plantation,—smiling at the workers in the cane-fields,—tempting men to follow her. But he who follows her never comes back again

claims.statement: In Hearn's chapter "La Guiablesse", none ever saw her by night; her hour is the fulness of the sun's flood-tide, and she comes in the dead hush and white flame of windless noons.
claims.statement_id: Dalam bab "La Guiablesse" karya Hearn, tidak ada yang pernah melihatnya pada malam hari; jamnya adalah puncak pasang surut matahari, ia datang dalam keheningan dan nyala putih tengah hari tanpa angin.
claims.quote: None ever saw her by night. Her hour is the fulness of the sun's flood-tide: she comes in the dead hush and white flame of windless noons

claims.statement: In Hearn's tale her face transforms into goblin horror and she shrieks with hideous laughter; he, smitten to the brain with the sight of her, reels, falls backward two thousand feet and dies upon the rocks of a mountain torrent.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah Hearn, wajahnya berubah menjadi kengerian mirip goblin dan ia menjerit dengan tawa mengerikan; "ia" yang terguncang oleh pemandangan wajahnya terhuyung, jatuh ke belakang sejauh dua ribu kaki, dan tewas di bebatuan sungai gunung.
claims.quote: the goblin horror of her face transformed,—shrieks with a burst of hideous laughter: ... smitten to the brain with the sight of her, reels, recoils, and, backward falling, crashes two thousand feet down to his death upon the rocks of a mountain torrent.

claims.statement: In the folklore of Trinidad and Tobago, the Lagahoo or Lugarhou is a mythical shapeshifting monster.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Trinidad and Tobago, Lagahoo atau Lugarhou adalah monster mitos pengubah wujud.
claims.quote: In the folklore of Trinidad and Tobago the Lagahoo or Lugarhou is a mythical shapeshifting monster.

claims.statement: By day it seems human, but at night it becomes a headless man roaming with a wooden coffin on its neck.
claims.statement_id: Pada siang hari ia tampak seperti manusia biasa, tetapi pada malam hari menjadi lelaki tanpa kepala yang berkeliaran dengan peti mati kayu di lehernya.
claims.quote: It seems like a normal human by day, but this creature takes on the form of a man with no head, who roams the night with a wooden coffin on its neck.

claims.statement: Three lit candles sit on the coffin, and a heavy iron chain tied at its waist trails behind.
claims.statement_id: Di atas peti itu ada tiga lilin menyala, dan rantai besi berat yang terikat di pinggangnya terseret di belakangnya.
claims.quote: On top of the coffin are three lighted candles and the long loose end of a heavy iron chain, noosed around its waist, trails behind him.

claims.statement: It can change into horses, pigs or goats and often takes a centaur-like form.
claims.statement_id: Ia dapat berubah menjadi berbagai hewan seperti kuda, babi, atau kambing, dan sering berwujud mirip centaur.
claims.quote: It can shapeshift into various animals, including horses, pigs or goats, and said to often take the form of a creature similar to a centaur

claims.statement: The Lagahoo can change its size from tiny to gigantic in an instant.
claims.statement_id: Lagahoo juga dapat mengubah ukurannya dari sangat kecil menjadi raksasa dalam sekejap.
claims.quote: The Lagahoo also possesses the ability to alter its size from tiny to gigantic in an instant.

claims.statement: To kill it, one must beat it with a stick anointed with holy water and holy oil for nine days.
claims.statement_id: Untuk membunuhnya, Lagahoo harus dipukuli dengan tongkat yang telah diurapi air suci dan minyak suci selama sembilan hari.
claims.quote: To kill the Lagahoo one must beat the creature with a stick which has been anointed with holy water and holy oil for nine days.

claims.statement: The Trinidadian version of the universal shape-shifter is the lagahoo; the word comes from the French loup-garou, meaning werewolf.
claims.statement_id: Versi Trinidad dari pengubah wujud universal adalah lagahoo; kata itu berasal dari bahasa Prancis loup-garou, yang berarti manusia serigala.
claims.quote: The Trinidadian version of the universal shape-shifter is the lagahoo — the word comes from the French loup-garou, meaning werewolf.

claims.statement: The poet James Aboud quotes Gerard Besson's Folklore of Trinidad as an epigraph: the Lagahoo could change his shape into any beast or form and roam the streets or forests.
claims.statement_id: Penyair James Aboud mengutip Folklore of Trinidad karya Gerard Besson sebagai epigraf: Lagahoo dapat mengubah wujudnya menjadi binatang atau bentuk apa pun dan berkeliaran di jalan atau hutan.
claims.quote: As an epigraph to his new book of poems, James Aboud quotes Gerard Besson’s Folklore of Trinidad: Lagahoo could change his shape into any beast or form and roam the streets or forests.

claims.statement: In the same quoted passage, to see him properly one had to put the yampee, or mucus from a dog's eye, in one's own eye and look through the keyhole at midnight.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kutipan folklor yang sama, untuk melihatnya dengan jelas orang harus mengoleskan yampee, yaitu lendir dari mata anjing, ke matanya sendiri lalu mengintip lewat lubang kunci pada tengah malam.
claims.quote: In order to see him properly, you had to put the yampee or mucus from a dog’s eye in your own eye and look through your keyhole at midnight.

claims.statement: In the same quoted passage, in everyday life he could be an Obeah man, or even a man of some learning, living a quiet, solitary life.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kutipan folklor yang sama, dalam kehidupan sehari-hari ia bisa menjadi seorang Obeah man, atau bahkan orang yang terpelajar, hidup tenang dan menyendiri.
claims.quote: In everyday life, he could be an Obeah man, or even a man of some learning, living a quiet, solitary life.

claims.statement: In the same quoted passage, he was a genius at maiming or killing, and people said that sometimes he became so tall that his head disappeared above the trees.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kutipan folklor yang sama, ia ahli melukai atau membunuh, dan konon kadang ia menjadi begitu tinggi sehingga kepalanya hilang di atas pepohonan.
claims.quote: He was a genius at maiming or killing. People said that sometimes he became so tall that his head disappeared above the trees.

claims.statement: The letiche is a creature of Cajun folklore in Louisiana, United States, that haunts the bayous (swamps).
claims.statement_id: Letiche adalah makhluk dalam cerita rakyat Cajun di Louisiana, Amerika Serikat, yang menghantui bayou (rawa).
claims.quote: The letiche is a creature in Cajun folklore in Louisiana, United States, which haunts the bayous (swamps).

claims.statement: It is described as the soul of an illegitimate unbaptized infant, or a child raised by alligators.
claims.statement_id: Ia digambarkan sebagai jiwa bayi haram yang tidak dibaptis, atau anak manusia yang dibesarkan buaya aligator.
claims.quote: It is variously described as the soul of an illegitimate unbaptized infant, or a human child raised by alligators.

claims.statement: The letiche lurks in the bayous, upsetting boats and attacking travelers.
claims.statement_id: Letiche konon mengintai di rawa, membalikkan perahu, dan menyerang pelancong.
claims.quote: The letiche is said to lurk in the bayous and upset boats and attack travelers.

claims.statement: In the poem Evangeline, a character tells children tales of the Loup-garou in the forest, of the goblin that came in the night to water the horses, and of the white Létiche, the ghost of a child who died unchristened and was doomed to haunt unseen the chambers of children.
claims.statement_id: Dalam puisi Evangeline, seorang tokoh menceritakan kepada anak-anak kisah Loup-garou di hutan, goblin yang datang malam hari untuk memberi minum kuda, dan Létiche putih, hantu anak yang meninggal tanpa dibaptis dan dikutuk menghantui kamar anak-anak tanpa terlihat.
claims.quote: For he told them tales of the Loup-garou in the forest, And of the goblin that came in the night to water the horses, And of the white Létiche, the ghost of a child who unchristened Died, and was doomed to haunt unseen the chambers of children;

claims.statement: Evangeline: A Tale of Acadie is by Henry Wadsworth Longfellow.
claims.statement_id: Evangeline: A Tale of Acadie adalah karya Henry Wadsworth Longfellow.
claims.quote: Title: Evangeline: A Tale of Acadie Author: Henry Wadsworth Longfellow

claims.statement: According to this compilation, the letiche is an animal whose form is scarcely defined, of dazzling whiteness, seen only at night and disappearing the moment anyone tries to touch it.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kompilasi ini, letiche adalah makhluk berwujud samar, putih menyilaukan, hanya terlihat pada malam hari, dan lenyap begitu ada yang mencoba menyentuhnya.
claims.quote: It is an animal whose form is scarcely defined, of dazzling whiteness, which is only seen in the night-time, and disappears the moment any one attempts to touch it.

claims.statement: According to this compilation, letiches are believed to be the souls of infants dead without baptism, and the compiler suggests this pretty little spirit was most probably no other than the agile and timid ermine of Normandy and Britanny (spelling as in the source).
claims.statement_id: Menurut kompilasi ini, letiche dipercaya sebagai jiwa bayi yang meninggal tanpa pembaptisan, dan penyusunnya menduga roh kecil ini kemungkinan besar tidak lain adalah ermine yang lincah dan pemalu dari Normandia dan Britanny (ejaan sumber).
claims.quote: souls of infants dead without baptism. Most probably this pretty little spirit was no other than the agile and timid ermine of Normandy and Britanny.

claims.statement: According to Encyclopedia Mythica, in superstitious belief at Bayeux, Normandy, the letiche is an animal of scarcely defined form and dazzling whiteness, seen only at night and disappearing when touched; letiches are believed to be the souls of infants who died without having been baptized.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Encyclopedia Mythica, dalam kepercayaan takhayul di Bayeux, Normandia, letiche adalah hewan berwujud samar, putih menyilaukan, hanya terlihat pada malam hari dan lenyap saat disentuh; letiche dipercaya sebagai jiwa bayi yang meninggal tanpa dibaptis.
claims.quote: In superstitious belief at Bayeux, Normandy, an animal whose form is scarcely defined, of dazzling whiteness, which is only seen at night time, and disappears the moment any one attempts to touch it. The letiches are believed to be the souls of infants who died without having been baptized.

claims.statement: The Madre de aguas ("Mother of water"), also known as Magüi, is a mythical creature of Cuban folklore.
claims.statement_id: Madre de aguas ("ibu air"), juga dikenal sebagai Magüi, adalah makhluk mitos dalam cerita rakyat Kuba.
claims.quote: The Madre de aguas (Mother of water), also known as Magüi, is a mythical creature in the folklore of Cuba.

claims.statement: In Creole folklore she is Mama Glo; on other islands she is Mami Wata or Watramama.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Kreol ia disebut Mama Glo, dan di pulau lain Mami Wata atau Watramama.
claims.quote: She goes by the name of Mama Glo in Creole Folklore, in other islands she is called Mami Wata as well as Watramama.

claims.statement: The story, first told in the 1600's, says she is a giant boa as thick as a palm tree.
claims.statement_id: Kisahnya pertama kali diceritakan pada tahun 1600-an: Madre de aguas adalah ular boa raksasa setebal pohon palem.
claims.quote: The story was first told in the 1600's and says that the Madre de aguas is a giant boa snake very large and wide with the thickness of a palm tree

claims.statement: She has two horn-like projections on her head and thick scales impenetrable to bullets.
claims.statement_id: Ia bertonjolan seperti dua tanduk di kepala dan bersisik tebal yang tak tembus peluru.
claims.quote: has two extrusions similar to horns in the frontal region of her head, and is covered in scales thick and distributed inversely as present in other boa snakes, which is impenetrable to bullets.

claims.statement: She inhabits rivers and lakes, which never dry while she lives there.
claims.statement_id: Ia konon menghuni sungai dan danau, yang tidak pernah kering selama ia tinggal di sana.
claims.quote: It is said that it inhabits rivers and lakes, which never dry out while it lives there.

claims.statement: The Madre de aguas never dies, and anyone who tries to kill or capture her dies.
claims.statement_id: Madre de aguas tidak pernah mati, dan siapa pun yang mencoba membunuh atau menangkapnya akan mati.
claims.quote: Madre de aguas never dies, and anyone who tries to kill or capture it dies.

claims.statement: An OnCubaNews editor's note quotes Feijóo in the book Mitología cubana (1986): in his research on the Cuban Madres de aguas he traveled through three provinces, Las Villas, Camaguey and La Habana.
claims.statement_id: Sebuah catatan editor OnCubaNews mengutip Feijóo dalam buku Mitología cubana (1986): dalam penelitiannya tentang Madres de aguas Kuba ia menempuh tiga provinsi, yaitu Las Villas, Camaguey, dan La Habana.
claims.quote: En el libro “Mitología cubana”, Ediciones Cubanas, 1986; Feijóo cuenta: “En nuestras investigaciones tras las Madres de aguas cubanas recorrimos tres provincias: Las Villas, Camaguey y La Habana,

claims.statement: In a quoted field testimony, a speaker says everyone tells him there is a Madre de aguas in the Laguna del Itabo, a snake with horns ("tarros"), and that the lagoon never dries up because it has a Madre de aguas.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kesaksian lapangan yang dikutip, seorang narasumber mengatakan semua orang bilang di Laguna del Itabo ada Madre de aguas, seekor ular bertanduk ("tarros"), dan laguna itu tidak pernah kering karena Madre de aguas tinggal di sana.
claims.quote: A mí me dice todo el mundo que aquí en la Laguna del Itabo hay un Madre de aguas, una serpiente con tarros. Esa laguna nunca se seca porque tiene Madre de aguas.

claims.statement: In the same testimony, fishermen are said to have grabbed it by hand but had to let it go because it pulls hard and was taking them down.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kesaksian yang sama, para nelayan konon pernah menangkapnya dengan tangan tetapi harus melepaskannya karena ia menarik kuat dan membawa mereka ke bawah.
claims.quote: pescadores que se han metido ahí, que hasta la han agarrado con la mano, y han tenido que soltarla porque ella jala mucho, y se los llevaba para abajo.

claims.statement: The mulher da meia-noite ("midnight woman") is a ghost of world folklore.
claims.statement_id: Mulher da meia-noite ("perempuan tengah malam") adalah hantu dalam cerita rakyat dunia.
claims.quote: A mulher da meia-noite é um fantasma do folclore mundial.

claims.statement: Her story has many variants worldwide, with the most varied accounts in South America.
claims.statement_id: Kisahnya punya banyak varian di berbagai belahan dunia, dan kisah paling beragam ditemukan di Amerika Selatan.
claims.quote: Sua história possui diversas variantes em várias partes do mundo, mas é na América do Sul que encontram relatos mais variados.

claims.statement: In Brazil she is also called Bela (or Dama) da Noite and A Mulher de branco ("the woman in white").
claims.statement_id: Di Brasil ia juga disebut Bela (atau Dama) da Noite dan A Mulher de branco ("perempuan berbaju putih").
claims.quote: No Brasil, a Mulher da meia-noite também recebe os nomes de Bela (ou Dama) da Noite, A Mulher de branco

claims.statement: In Venezuela she is called "La Sayona".
claims.statement_id: Di Venezuela ia disebut "La Sayona".
claims.quote: Na Venezuela, é chamada de "La Sayona".

claims.statement: In Mexico she was named "La Llorona".
claims.statement_id: Di Meksiko ia dinamai "La Llorona".
claims.quote: No México recebeu o nome de "La Llorona"

claims.statement: One Brazilian version: a beautiful young woman who appears on roads asking men for rides.
claims.statement_id: Salah satu versi Brasil: perempuan muda cantik yang muncul di jalan dan meminta tumpangan kepada laki-laki.
claims.quote: Uma bela jovem que aparece em estradas e pede carona para os homens.

claims.statement: If the man truly betrays his partner she may kill him; otherwise she only wounds him.
claims.statement_id: Jika laki-laki itu benar-benar berselingkuh, ia dapat membunuhnya; jika tidak, ia hanya melukainya.
claims.quote: Se ele realmente trair, ela poderá matá-lo; caso contrário, ela apenas irá feri-lo.

claims.statement: Portal do Trânsito writes that the legend of the woman in white has many variants in various parts of the world, and in Brazil she is also called Bela da Noite or Mulher da meia-noite.
claims.statement_id: Portal do Trânsito menulis bahwa legenda perempuan berbaju putih punya banyak varian di berbagai belahan dunia, dan di Brasil ia juga disebut Bela da Noite atau Mulher da meia-noite.
claims.quote: A assustadora lenda da mulher de branco possui diversas variantes em várias partes do mundo. No Brasil, a mulher de branco também recebe os nomes de Bela da Noite ou Mulher da meia-noite.

claims.statement: One of the main versions tells of a young woman dressed as a bride who appears on roads, asking lone drivers for a ride and for help getting home.
claims.statement_id: Salah satu versi utamanya menceritakan seorang gadis berpakaian seperti pengantin yang muncul di jalan, meminta tumpangan kepada pengemudi yang sendirian dan meminta bantuan untuk pulang.
claims.quote: Uma das principais versões conta a lenda de uma jovem vestida como uma noiva. Ela aparece em estradas pedindo carona para motoristas solitários e pedindo ajuda para voltar para casa.

claims.statement: As they pass in front of a cemetery, she suddenly disappears from inside the car, leaving the drivers confused and terrified. The apparition is supposedly the spirit of a bride who died in an accident on the eve of her wedding.
claims.statement_id: Ketika mereka melewati sebuah pemakaman, ia mendadak lenyap dari dalam mobil dan membuat pengemudi bingung dan ketakutan. Konon penampakan itu adalah roh seorang pengantin yang tewas dalam kecelakaan pada malam sebelum pernikahannya.
claims.quote: No momento que passam em frente a algum cemitério, ela desaparece subitamente de dentro do carro, deixando os motoristas confusos e apavorados. Supostamente, a assombração seria a manifestação do espírito de uma noiva que morreu em um acidente na véspera de seu casamento.

claims.statement: Mixtecatl is one of the six giant sons of Iztac-Mixcoatl and Tlaltecuhtli (or Ilancueitl) who populated the Earth after the Great Flood in the Fifth Sun of Aztec mythology.
claims.statement_id: Mixtecatl adalah salah satu dari enam raksasa putra Iztac-Mixcoatl dan Tlaltecuhtli (atau Ilancueitl) yang menghuni Bumi setelah Air Bah pada masa Matahari Kelima dalam mitologi Aztek.
claims.quote: Mixtecatl (From Nahuatl, 'Inhabitant of the land of clouds') is one of the six giants sons of Iztac-Mixcoatl and Tlaltecuhtli or Ilancueitl that populated the Earth after the Great Flood during the Fifth Sun in Aztec mythology.

claims.statement: He was the fifth son, founder of Mixtlan, origin of the people of the region now called Mixteca.
claims.statement_id: Ia putra kelima yang mendirikan Mixtlan, asal penduduk wilayah yang kini disebut Mixteca.
claims.quote: The fifth son who founded Mixtlan from where the natives of the region known today as Mixteca come from.

claims.statement: In this Nahoa cosmogony poem, a being of many jaws and bloody tongues, by a metamorphosis, is sanctified and takes the rare name of Ilancuéye.
claims.statement_id: Dalam puisi kosmogoni Nahoa ini, sosok berahang banyak dan berlidah berdarah, lewat suatu metamorfosis, disucikan dan mengambil nama langka Ilancuéye.
claims.quote: With many jaws and bloody tongues; By such a metamorphosis is sanctified, And takes the rare name of Ilancuéye:

claims.statement: In the poem, the "ferocious serpent of white cloud" who lives in Citlálco is joined with her, six tlacámes (men) are engendered, and these brothers dwell on the earth and become the source of many races.
claims.statement_id: Dalam puisi itu, "ular ganas dari awan putih" yang tinggal di Citlálco bersatu dengannya, dan persatuan itu melahirkan enam tlacámes (laki-laki); saudara-saudara ini hidup di bumi dan menjadi sumber banyak bangsa.
claims.quote: the «ferocious serpent Of white cloud» which lives in Citlálco, (24) With her is joined in sweet union, Of love, which six tlacámes engender; (25) These brothers dwell on the earth And become the source of many races:

claims.statement: In the poem, the valiant Mixtécatl guards himself from Mixtecápan in the barren hills; footnote 32 states that it is today called simply Mixteca.
claims.statement_id: Dalam puisi itu, Mixtécatl yang gagah berani berlindung dari Mixtecápan di perbukitan tandus; catatan kaki 32 menyatakan bahwa kini ia disebut sederhana Mixteca.
claims.quote: The valiant Mixtécatl guards himself From Mixtecápan in the barren hills; (32) ... (32) Today is called simply Mixteca.

claims.statement: A footnote in the same book explains that the name Iztamixcóhuatl is composed of iztac (white), mixtli (cloud) and cohuatl (serpent).
claims.statement_id: Catatan kaki dalam buku yang sama menjelaskan bahwa nama Iztamixcóhuatl tersusun dari iztac (putih), mixtli (awan), dan cohuatl (ular).
claims.quote: Iztamixcóhuatl is composed of iztac, white, mixtli, cloud, and cohuatl, serpent;

claims.statement: A footnote explains that Ilancueye means "old frog" and says Mr. Orozco y Berra, following Torquemada, fell into the error of calling this goddess Ilancueitl.
claims.statement_id: Catatan kaki menjelaskan bahwa Ilancueye berarti "katak tua" dan menyebut Orozco y Berra, mengikuti Torquemada, keliru menyebut sang dewi Ilancueitl.
claims.quote: Ilancueye is composed of ilamatl or ilantli, old, and of cueye, corruption of cueyatl, "frog; old frog." Mr. Orozco y Berra, following Torquemada, fell into the error of calling this goddess Ilancueitl

claims.statement: A footnote in the same book says the Indians believed the earth was first inhabited by giants, and that the large fossilized bones found in excavations were their remains; they called them quinametzin.
claims.statement_id: Catatan kaki dalam buku yang sama menyatakan bahwa orang Indian percaya bumi pertama kali dihuni raksasa, dan tulang besar fosil yang ditemukan dalam penggalian dianggap sisa mereka; mereka menyebutnya quinametzin.
claims.quote: The Indians believed that the earth was first inhabited by giants, and the large pachyderm bones that were found in a fossilized state in excavations, were their remains. They called them quinametzin,

claims.statement: Otomitl is one of the six giant sons of Iztac-Mixcoatl and Tlaltecuhtli who populated the Earth after the Great Flood in the Fifth Sun of Aztec mythology.
claims.statement_id: Otomitl adalah salah satu dari enam raksasa putra Iztac-Mixcoatl dan Tlaltecuhtli yang menghuni Bumi setelah Air Bah pada masa Matahari Kelima dalam mitologi Aztek.
claims.quote: Otomitl (From Nahuatl, 'Jute bone' or 'Where the otomies are') is one of the six giants sons of Iztac-Mixcoatl and Tlaltecuhtli that populated the Earth after the Great Flood during the Fifth Sun in Aztec mythology.

claims.statement: He was the sixth son, who climbed the mountains near Mexico and raised the settlements of Xilotepec, Tollan and Otompan.
claims.statement_id: Ia putra keenam yang mendaki pegunungan dekat Mexico dan membangun permukiman Xilotepec, Tollan, dan Otompan.
claims.quote: The sixth son who climbed the mountains near Mexico, and raised the populations of Xilotepec, Tollan, and Otompan.

claims.statement: In this Nahoa cosmogony poem, the "ferocious serpent of white cloud" who lives in Citlálco is joined with her, six tlacámes (men) are engendered, and these brothers dwell on the earth and become the source of many races.
claims.statement_id: Dalam puisi kosmogoni Nahoa ini, "ular ganas dari awan putih" yang tinggal di Citlálco bersatu dengannya, enam tlacáme (laki-laki) lahir, dan saudara-saudara itu tinggal di bumi serta menjadi sumber banyak bangsa.
claims.quote: the «ferocious serpent Of white cloud» which lives in Citlálco, (24) With her is joined in sweet union, Of love, which six tlacámes engender; (25) These brothers dwell on the earth And become the source of many races:

claims.statement: A footnote in the same book says the Indians believed the earth was first inhabited by giants, and that the large fossilized bones found in excavations were their remains; they called them quinametzin.
claims.statement_id: Catatan kaki dalam buku yang sama menyebut bahwa orang Indian percaya bumi mula-mula dihuni raksasa, dan tulang besar yang ditemukan dalam keadaan fosil di galian dianggap sisa-sisa mereka; mereka menyebutnya quinametzin.
claims.quote: The Indians believed that the earth was first inhabited by giants, and the large pachyderm bones that were found in a fossilized state in excavations, were their remains. They called them quinametzin,

claims.statement: The poem names the six brothers in turn: Xélhua the firstborn (a giant), Tenoch, Ulmécatl, Xicaláncatl, Mixtécatl, and Otómitl, "the Xocóyotl".
claims.statement_id: Puisi itu menyebut keenam bersaudara berurutan: Xélhua si sulung (raksasa), Tenoch, Ulmécatl, Xicaláncatl, Mixtécatl, dan Otómitl, "Xocóyotl".
claims.quote: The firstborn, the giant Xélhua, ... Tenoch, the great ... The strong Cuetlaxcoápan founded Ulmécatl; ... Xicaláncatl; ... The valiant Mixtécatl guards himself ... Otómitl, the Xocóyotl, lives ever

claims.statement: Robelo's footnote says Xocóyotl means "the last son", and that the Aztec expression "socoyote" was formed from this word.
claims.statement_id: Catatan kaki buku itu menyatakan bahwa Xocóyotl berarti "putra terakhir", dan dari kata itu terbentuk ungkapan Aztek "socoyote".
claims.quote: Xocóyotl means “the last son.“ From this word was formed the Aztec expression

claims.statement: In Robelo's poem, Otómitl, the Xocóyotl, lives always in the mountains around Mexico and prospers in rich populations such as Túllan, Xilatepéc and Otómpan.
claims.statement_id: Dalam puisi itu, Otómitl, sang Xocóyotl, selalu tinggal di pegunungan di sekitar Mexico dan makmur di permukiman padat seperti Túllan, Xilatepéc, dan Otómpan.
claims.quote: Otómitl, the Xocóyotl, lives ever ... In the mountains that lie around Mexico And there prospers in rich populations, Such as Túllan, of wisdom the emporium, Xilatepéc and Otómpan, of labor.

claims.statement: Robelo's footnote states that these populations now carry the names Tula, Jilotepec and Otumba, and all belong to the state of Hidalgo.
claims.statement_id: Catatan kaki buku itu menyatakan bahwa permukiman-permukiman itu kini bernama Tula, Jilotepec, dan Otumba, dan semuanya termasuk negara bagian Hidalgo.
claims.quote: These populations now carry the names of Tula, Jilotepec, Otumba and all belong to the state of Hidalgo.

claims.statement: The Pincoy is a male sea water spirit of Chilote mythology in Chiloé, Chile.
claims.statement_id: Pincoy adalah roh air laut laki-laki dalam mitologi Chilote di Chiloé, Chile.
claims.quote: The Pincoy is a  male water spirit of the seas, belonging to the Chilote mythology of Chiloé, Chile.

claims.statement: He resembles a merman with a large golden sea-lion body, a handsome face and long golden hair, magically attractive to women.
claims.statement_id: Ia mirip manusia duyung laki-laki bertubuh seperti singa laut besar berwarna emas, berwajah tampan, berambut emas panjang, dan memikat perempuan secara gaib.
claims.quote: It looks equivalent to a merman creature, his body would be like a large sea lion, colour bright golden, with handsome and manly human face and long golden hair, being magically attractive to the women.

claims.statement: He is the son of Millalobo, king of the seas, and the human Huenchula; his sisters are the Sirena chilota and the Pincoya, who is also his wife.
