claims.statement: Ahöla, also Ahul, is a spirit being (kachina) of Hopi religion, embodied by a man.
claims.statement_id: Ahöla, juga Ahul, adalah makhluk roh (kachina) dalam agama Hopi yang diperankan oleh seorang laki-laki.
claims.quote: Ahöla, also known as Ahul,  is a spirit being, a kachina, embodied by a man, in Hopi religion.

claims.statement: Ahöla is an important chief katsinam for First and Second Mesas, opening the mid-winter Powamu ceremony, the bean planting festival.
claims.statement_id: Ahöla adalah salah satu katsinam kepala yang penting bagi First dan Second Mesa karena ia membuka upacara pertengahan musim dingin Powamu, festival menanam kacang.
claims.quote: Ahöla is one of the important chief katsinam for First and Second Mesas because he opens the mid-winter Powamu ceremony, sometimes called the bean planting festival.

claims.statement: At the end, Ahöla goes to a shrine, bows four times to the sun and asks for health, happiness, long life and good crops.
claims.statement_id: Di akhir upacara, Ahöla turun ke sebuah tempat suci, membungkuk empat kali kepada matahari, dan memohon kesehatan, kebahagiaan, umur panjang, dan panen yang baik.
claims.quote: At the end of the ceremony, Ahöla descends to a shrine, bows four times to the sun, and asks for health, happiness, long life, and good crops.

claims.statement: Ahöla is also the friend of Eototo.
claims.statement_id: Ahöla juga sahabat Eototo.
claims.quote: Ahöla is also the friend of Eototo

claims.statement: In the note on a Hopi painting of the Soyal ritual, Ahola comes over to a house; the man of the house speaks to him and the kachina merely gestures.
claims.statement_id: Dalam keterangan lukisan Hopi tentang upacara Soyal, Ahola datang ke sebuah rumah; tuan rumah berbicara kepadanya, dan kachina itu hanya memberi isyarat.
claims.quote: An additional ritual part of Soyal is depicted. ... Ahola comes over to the house." The man of the house speaks to the kachina who merely gestures.

claims.statement: According to the note, Ahola Mana follows Ahola carrying seeds of various types from the fields of the Kachina Chief.
claims.statement_id: Menurut keterangan itu, Ahola Mana mengikuti Ahola sambil membawa berbagai jenis biji dari ladang Kachina Chief.
claims.quote: Following Ahola, Ahola Mana carries seeds of various types from the fields of the Kachina Chief.

claims.statement: The book gives Ahola Wotaka, "Old Man Ahola," as described by another viewer of the painting.
claims.statement_id: Buku itu menyebut Ahola Wotaka, "Old Man Ahola", sebagaimana dijelaskan oleh seorang penonton lukisan.
claims.quote: Ahola Wotaka, "Old Man Ahola," was described by another viewer:

claims.statement: One viewer says Ahola is the first to come in February, wobbling around because he was just wakened, and after he goes home Soyal Kachina comes in.
claims.statement_id: Seorang penonton lukisan berkata bahwa Ahola yang pertama datang pada bulan Februari, berjalan terhuyung-huyung karena baru dibangunkan, dan setelah ia pulang barulah Soyal Kachina datang.
claims.quote: "Ahola is the first one that comes in February. He wobbles around because he was just wakened and after he goes home Soyal Kachina comes in

claims.statement: The same viewer says they come to the headman of the kiva and he prays to Ahola and Aholmana.
claims.statement_id: Penonton yang sama berkata bahwa mereka datang kepada kepala kiva, yang berdoa kepada Ahola dan Aholmana.

claims.statement: Legend says the Negro-d'Água or Nego-d'Água inhabits many rivers, such as the Tocantins, Rio Grande and São Francisco.
claims.statement_id: Menurut legenda, Negro-d'Água atau Nego-d'Água menghuni banyak sungai, seperti Rio Tocantins, Rio Grande, dan Rio São Francisco.
claims.quote: Diz a lenda que o Negro-d'Água ou Nego-d'Água habita diversos rios, tais como o Rio Tocantins, o Rio Grande, Rio Grande, oeste da Bahia e Rio São Francisco

claims.statement: It appears laughing loudly, bald, with duck-like hands and feet, and capsizes the canoes of fishermen who refuse it a fish.
claims.statement_id: Ia muncul dengan tawa terbahak-bahak, berkepala botak, bertangan dan berkaki seperti bebek, dan membalikkan kano nelayan yang menolak memberinya ikan.
claims.quote: Manifestando-se com suas gargalhadas, negro, careca e com mãos e pés de pato, ele derruba a canoa dos pescadores, se eles se recusarem a lhe dar um peixe.

claims.statement: Some fishermen throw a bottle of cachaça into the river so their boat is not overturned.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian nelayan melempar sebotol cachaça ke sungai agar perahunya tidak dibalikkan.
claims.quote: levam uma garrafa de cachaça e a atiram para dentro do rio, para que não tenham sua embarcação virada.

claims.statement: It is a fusion of a tall, strong man and an amphibian, with fins and scales mixed with skin.
claims.statement_id: Wujudnya perpaduan lelaki tinggi kuat dengan amfibi, bersirip, dan bertubuh bersisik bercampur kulit.
claims.quote: ele seria a fusão de homem negro alto e forte com um anfíbio. Apresenta nadadeiras e corpo coberto de escamas mistas com a pele.

claims.statement: Câmara Cascudo calls it "Negro do Rio" and considers it derived from the Ipupiara.
claims.statement_id: Câmara Cascudo menyebutnya "Negro do Rio" dan menganggapnya turunan Ipupiara.
claims.quote: Câmara Cascudo chama-o "Negro do Rio" e o considera um derivado do Ipupiara.

claims.statement_id: Dalam verbete Caboclo-d'Água, Cascudo mencatat Negro-d'água di antara nama lain makhluk itu dan mengutip uraian José A. Teixeira (Folclore Goiano) tentangnya.

claims.statement: In the passage by Teixeira quoted by Cascudo, the Negro-d'água inhabits the banks of rivers running through the Paraná valley; it is all black, bald-headed, with duck hands and feet.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kutipan Teixeira yang dimuat Cascudo, Negro-d'água mendiami tepi sungai-sungai yang mengalir di lembah Paraná; ia serba hitam, berkepala botak, bertangan dan berkaki bebek.
claims.quote: Habita as mar- gens dos rios que correm pelo vão do Paraná. É todo preto. Cabeça pelada. Mãos e pés de pato.

claims.statement: According to the passage, it appears among rocks (pedras) at dusk (à tardinha) or on moonlit nights (noites de luar) to canoeists and fishermen, and tries to overturn the canoe (virar a canoa).
claims.statement_id: Menurut kutipan itu, ia muncul di antara bebatuan (pedras) pada senja (à tardinha) atau malam berbulan purnama (noites de luar) kepada pendayung kano dan nelayan, dan berusaha membalikkan kano (virar a canoa).
claims.quote: Aparece entre pedras, à tardinha ou em noites de luar, a canoeiros e pescadores do ... e seus afluentes. E procura virar a canoa.

claims.statement: According to the passage, shooting at it is foolish: the bullet strikes the hairy hide of the black one.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kutipan itu, menembaknya sia-sia karena peluru memantul dari kulit berbulu si hitam.
claims.quote: É bobagem atirar bala: bate no couro peludo do negro

claims.statement: In the mythology of the Quechua of Ecuador, Amarum is a spirit shaped like a water boa that brings rain.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi orang Quechua di Ekuador, Amarum adalah roh berwujud ular boa air yang membawa hujan.
claims.quote: In the mythology of the Quechua people of Ecuador, Amarum is a spirit in the shape of a water boa that bring rain.

claims.statement: Bonnerjea's dictionary describes Amarum as one of the most formidable demons known among the Quichas of Ecuador, in the form of a huge water boa.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Kamus Takhayul dan Mitologi karya Bonnerjea, Amarum disebut sebagai salah satu iblis paling menakutkan di kalangan orang Quichas di Ekuador dan berwujud ular boa air raksasa.
claims.quote: Among the Quichas of Equador this is one of the most formidable demons known; it is of the form of a huge water-boa.

claims.statement: According to the entry, Amarum is the father of witchcraft, and the souls of sorcerers are said to take up their abode in these monsters.
claims.statement_id: Menurut entri itu, Amarum adalah bapak ilmu sihir, dan arwah para dukun santet dikatakan berdiam di dalam makhluk-makhluk ini.
claims.quote: It is the father of witchcraft, and the souls of sorcerers are said to take up their abode in these monsters.

claims.statement: Bonnerjea's entry on Amarum cites Karsten, Indian Tribes of Equador, page 70, as its reference.
claims.statement_id: Entri Bonnerjea tentang Amarum mencantumkan Karsten, Indian Tribes of Equador, halaman 70, sebagai rujukannya.
claims.quote: (KARSTEN, Indian Tribes of Equador, P. 70.)

claims.statement: Karsten writes that the anaconda is the principal and most feared of all the demons that people the spiritual world of the Ecuadorian Indians, and that it is the father of witchcraft.
claims.statement_id: Karsten menulis bahwa anakonda adalah yang utama dan paling ditakuti di antara semua iblis yang mendiami dunia roh orang Indian Ekuador, dan bahwa ia adalah bapak ilmu sihir.
claims.quote: The anaconda, in fact, is the principal and the most feared of all the demons that people the spiritual world of the Ecuadorian Indians. He is the father of witchcraft.

claims.statement: Karsten writes that the souls of medicine-men are supposed to be able to transmigrate into the anaconda, both after death and in life, and that when the Indians kill such a monster they say they have killed an evil sorcerer.
claims.statement_id: Karsten menulis bahwa jiwa para dukun dianggap dapat berpindah ke dalam anakonda, baik setelah mati maupun semasa hidup, dan bahwa orang Indian yang membunuh makhluk itu mengatakan telah membunuh seorang dukun jahat.
claims.quote: Both after death and in their lifetime the souls of the medicine-men are supposed to be able to transmigrate into the anaconda; and when the Indians kill such a monster they say that they have killed an evil sorcerer.
